reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Since August 2026 dispute tickets have doubled (E-07), and the surge is substantially driven by errors in processing bills built from ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads: 59% of 3025 disputed bills carry read_type=ACTUAL vs 41% ESTIMATED (E-03), ruling out estimate-substitution/field-read failure as the dominant mechanism. Tariff changes are ruled out (zero logged changes, E-02) and ticket response handling is already within SLA (E-04), so this is not a response-speed problem; the specific defect inside actual-read bill processing (e.g. an import/validation rule change) is not yet pinpointed.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Since August 2026, dispute ticket volume has roughly doubled (from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep, E-07). A significant driver is billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), which compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling; firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report registers in 0.1 m3 units rather than m3 (E-13), so BV-17 misclassifies their normal consumption as high and rejects the read (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) at billing import, forcing estimate substitution. This exact pattern accounts for 1184 of the 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read-type bills (E-11). Whether the same mechanism (or a different one) also explains the 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read-type bills (59% of 3025 disputed bills, E-03) is not yet established.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
